Days Of The New.biography: Days of the New is an American rock band from Charlestown, Indiana, formed in 1995. The band consists of vocalist/guitarist Travis Meeks and a variety of supporting musicians. They are best known for the hit singles "Touch, Peel and Stand", "The Down Town", "Shelf in the Room", and "Enemy".

perplexity.description:
Days of the New is the debut album by the American rock band Days of the New, released in 1997. It is known for its distinctive dark acoustic rock style, which set it apart from the prevalent electric rock of the time. The album features a dozen tracks written by lead vocalist and guitarist Travis Meeks, including hit singles like "Touch, Peel and Stand," "The Down Town," and "Shelf in the Room." The production, led by Scott Litt (noted for his work with R.E.M. and Nirvana), emphasizes acoustic guitars and moody atmospherics, creating a sound that blends raw rock energy with a more introspective, acoustic-driven approach.

This album holds a significant place in Days of the New's discography as the first of three self-titled releases, often referred to by the color of its cover and disc as the "Yellow" or "Orange" album. It was both a critical and commercial success, selling over 1.5 million copies worldwide and achieving platinum status in the U.S. Its lead single, "Touch, Peel and Stand," was particularly acclaimed, holding the number one spot on Billboard's Mainstream Rock chart for 17 weeks and later being named the "Greatest of All-Time Mainstream Rock Song" by Billboard. The album's acoustic rock style and strong songwriting have allowed it to maintain relevance and respect over the decades since its release.
